$comment: Kit config scaffold (conventions: commands.* are npm script names (e.g. build), not commands - install and sync refuse a value like "npm run build" (commands.lintStaged and commands.logQuery are the full commands); commands.dev is the npm script that serves the frontend in a slot (no such script = no frontend); slots.fePorts/bePorts are BASE port numbers (main = base, slot N = base+N); slots.fePortArgs are appended to the frontend start command, {port} = the slot's port, and must make the dev server FAIL when the port is taken, never move to another port - the default [--port, {port}] is only right for a server that already fails on a busy port; one that moves to the next free port needs its strict-port flag added (install and sync print a NOTE while commands.dev is set and every slots.fe* value is the default); slots.feExec (optional) runs that binary with npm exec -- instead of the commands.dev script; slots.feMatcher is a regex for the dev server's processes (default: run <commands.dev>); slots.feEnvFile (optional) is a local environment file the frontend needs - its slot copy (.local -> .slot) gets the slot's backend port; paths.srcRoot/serverRoot end with a slash when set; slots.dbNameFormat is a JS template body with ${n}; paths.hotspots is a list, rendered per context; project.i18nFile is a file, a glob or a folder (a trailing slash means everything under it), or a comma-separated list - every entry is an append-only hotspot; plans.openDirs lists the folders whose *.plan.md files are open plans - range folders like plans/300-400/ are never open; project.repoName is the repo folder name (default: the target folder name) used for slot folders and base hrefs; slots.dbBackupDir defaults to <project slug>-db-backups; paths.routesFile is the router config file; paths.planChecks is the project's own planning checklist that /plan's Architect + PM review adds when the file exists (optional; the kit never writes it); security.sensitivePaths: a regex string replaces ship-prep's built-in sensitive-path regex, a list of globs is added to it (and fills the Cursor security rule globs); tools.browser names the browser tool (left at the default, AGENTS.md does not name one); overrides is a list of { path, reason } for installed files the project keeps as its own - install skips them, sync reports them as override and never writes them; listing AGENTS.md there makes the kit write its rules to AGENTS.workflow.md, which CLAUDE.md imports). ci.install is the command CI installs the app dependencies with (default npm ci; e.g. npm install --no-audit --no-fund when the lockfile is not the project's to fix); ci.lintScope all runs npm run <commands.lint>, changed runs ESLint on the changed *.ts *.tsx *.js *.jsx *.mjs *.cjs files only, kit-managed files left out (vs the PR base; a push compares with the commit before it); ci.appAuditMode enforce fails the security workflow on a critical production advisory, report writes the findings to the job summary and a warning instead (the kit-managed scripts/ dependencies are audited report-only: a kit release fixes them); ci.testMode run (default) runs npm run <commands.test> in the test job, if-present runs it with --if-present (no such script = pass), skip renders no test job; any other value of the three modes is refused by install and sync; paths.serverRoot empty = no backend job or step in CI; commands.logQuery (optional) is the full command that prints the errors the app logged since the plan started - /review-it then runs it as a Logs check (unset = no Logs check); project.uiLocale is a display phrase for sentences (e.g. Arabic RTL), not a locale code; project.uiDirection rtl makes the styling skill say the UI runs right-to-left, naming project.uiLocale when set (rtl, ltr or empty); commands.logQuery may not contain a pipe or a backtick; project.icons.library / component / registry name the icon library, the component a template imports for it and the file icons are registered in - set all three and the angular pack's component skill and conventions name them instead of the generic project icon registry; docs.domainSummary (optional) is a one-line list of the core domain rules, which the angular standards doc's Logic line then names instead of pointing at docs.domainStandards; stack.conventionsDoc, backendDoc, styleSkill, authSkill, docsMapSkill, docsMapCheck, cssSection, componentsSection are the pack contract - a stack pack (or a layer) fills them from its provides (a project may set its own) and core leaves out what is unset; stack.packs and stack.layers name the stack packs and the layers (supabase, upstream-owned; the Cursor layer is --cursor) - install records them, and with no --packs and no stack.packs it detects them from the project, prints why, and installs only after --yes; ownership.upstreamPaths are globs of the files an upstream repo owns (the upstream-owned layer sets .gitignore, AGENTS.md, package.json, package-lock.json; a project list replaces it) - install never writes them, sync and drift-check report them as override, and the scope guard denies them in a slot, even when a plan lists them. models.mechanical / analysis / judgment / build / review are the model tiers the kit's sub-agents and forked skills run on (docs/agent/model-routing.md): mechanical runs commands and reports facts (default haiku), analysis gathers evidence with file:line (default sonnet), judgment is for roles that decide (default opus; INV-1: never inherit and never Haiku - install and sync refuse both), build is for agents that write code (default sonnet; a builder that fails escalates to the judgment tier), review is for the validating agents - the checkers, the verifier, the security and UI validators (default sonnet, or the project's own models.analysis when it set that and not review - a Haiku analysis gives sonnet; never Haiku: install and sync refuse haiku or a claude-haiku- id for it); a value is haiku, sonnet, opus, fable, inherit or a full model id starting claude- - install and sync refuse anything else; the other tiers may be inherit (the main session's model), judgment may not. orchestrator.* tunes the opt-in orchestrator run (/orchestrate, docs/agent/orchestrator.md): runBranchPrefix is the prefix of the run branch every plan of a run merges into (default orch/; lower-case letters, digits, dots, dashes and slashes, ending with a slash - never the main branch), maxFixRounds is how many times a plan's problems go back to a builder before the plan is parked (an integer 1-5, default 2), minFreeDiskGb is the free disk the environment check asks for before a run and before a retry (a number of GB, 0-1000, default 5) - install and sync refuse any other value naming the key. commands.testCi (optional, an npm script name) is the test command the orchestrator gate runs instead of commands.test - set it when commands.test is a watch mode that never exits (e.g. a test:ci script running ng test --watch=false); project.packageManager is npm (default) or pnpm and picks the install and run commands that CI, the slots and the orchestrator use (a pnpm project keeps its own pnpm-lock.yaml); orchestrator.gateTimeoutMin stops a gate command that runs longer (1-120 minutes, default 15), orchestrator.builderIdleMin stops one builder call of scripts/run-plans.mjs only after that many minutes with no file changed in its folder (1-120, else 15; no wall-clock limit; a builder stopped idle parks with its work kept on park/<run>-<NNN>), orchestrator.concurrency caps parallel builders of the workflow (1-3, default 2; scripts/run-plans.mjs runs one plan at a time unless --concurrency 2 is given) and orchestrator.useSlots (true or false, default true) lets a run build in an idle wt-N slot before it creates its own folder, and orchestrator.watchTestPattern (optional) is a regular expression for the project's own framework's watch-mode test command: when the gate's test script matches it, the preflight prints a WARN gate line (jest --watch and vitest without run are always recognised). orchestrator.staleMin (1-240, default 10) is how many minutes without a status.json update make orch-state.mjs watch print STUCK. orchestrator.mergeChecks (default build) is what the merge step runs on the merged tree before it commits: build = the project build plus the plan's own scope check (lint and tests passed in the plan's gate and run once more at the final gate on the run branch), full = the plan's whole check list on every merge; install and sync refuse any other value. orchestrator.onPark (default dependents) is what a parked plan stops: dependents = only the later plans that depend on it or share its files, all = every later plan (the behaviour before plan 042); install and sync refuse any other value. orchestrator.prepare (list, default []) holds { "missing": "<repo-relative path>", "script": "<npm script>", "in": "<repo-relative folder, default .>" } entries: each becomes a first gate command (node scripts/orch-state.mjs prepare) of every plan gate and of the final gate that runs the script only when the path is absent, so a fresh worktree or the merge folder gets a generated folder before the tests; install and sync refuse an absolute path, a .., a script that is a full command or an unknown field. The per-plan gate also runs node scripts/kit-manifest-check.mjs when the project has a kit manifest (the merge step does not). orchestrator.ciMirror (list, default []) names CI commands (npm run <script>, pnpm run <script>, node scripts/<file>.mjs or node tools/<file>.mjs, no write flags) that the final gate runs after the project checks and the kit manifest check, so a green run is a green PR; install and sync only print a NOTE ci-mirror line for a workflow command not covered, they never write it. scripts/run-plans.mjs (the orchestrator as one script, plan 088) reads three more: orchestrator.reviewerMode (default gate) is what a STOP of the single reviewer does - advisory = recorded, the plan still merges; gate = a fix round, then the plan parks (a review that could not run parks too); advisory applies only to a plan whose Execution Mode says Reviewer: advisory (any other plan is reviewed as gate) and never to a diff that touches a sensitive path (ship-prep's check, security.sensitivePaths included), which is always gate; orchestrator.reviewerModel (default sonnet - Human 2026-11-07, until the fixed eval of plan 091 says otherwise) is the model run-plans.mjs runs .claude/agents/plan-reviewer.md on (passed as --model; the agent's own model: line stays models.review) - never Haiku (install and sync refuse it); orchestrator.rateLimitWaitMin (0-600, default 30) is how long a run pauses after a rate or usage limit before it retries the call once (a second limit stops the run). The old workflow keys orchestrator.pilotSize, fallbackModel, maxNotesPerPlan, maxAgentCallsPerPlan, triage, triageMinAgreement and triageMinGraded are removed: install and sync ignore a project value with one NOTE orchestrator: <key> removed line each. mods.enabled lists the Claude Code mods the project turns on (fleet, guards, ship-pilot; default none - install and sync refuse other names) and mods.marketplaceRepo is the <owner>/<repo> that serves them (the kit's own repository by default): with a mod enabled, install and sync write the marketplace (auto-updating) and one enabledPlugins entry per mod into .claude/settings.json; the mods read the hotspots and port bases the kit rendered from these keys (scripts/scope-check.mjs, scripts/lib/slot.mjs). Core files reference these keys as {{dotted.key}}. Values here are placeholders; each project fills its own. Generic defaults are kept only for git.mainBranch, the slot naming/count, slots.fePortArgs and the docs paths (paths.sharedDocs, paths.planChecks). brain.projectId (default project.repoName) is the short name a run's evidence is filed under in the kit brain, and brain.enabled (default true) turns the send off; a brain.* value is never a connection string - install and sync refuse one: the connection string lives in the KIT_BRAIN_URI environment variable (docs/agent/kit-brain.md). review.ship (default checkers) is what a REGULAR /ship on a plan branch reviews with: checkers = the /review-it checker pipeline (finders and verifier on models.review), reviewer = the single reviewer (scripts/lib/plan-review.mjs, one headless call of .claude/agents/plan-reviewer.md), light = the single /review pass; /ship fast picks light unless the diff touches a sensitive path. review.learn (default off) turns on the /ship learning step: on = /ship lists the decisions to grade, runs the grade and learning step (docs/agent/decision-review.md) and proposes brain entries; off = none of the three. install and sync refuse any other value of either key. commands.devRemote (optional, an npm script name, default dev:remote) is the backend script on the remote database: the orchestrator preflight runs it in server/ instead of commands.devLocal (default dev:local) when /orchestrate is given the word remote; the preflight starts the main folder's frontend (commands.dev) and, for a plan with an [auto:main] item, its backend through scripts/slot-serve.mjs --main.

ui.$comment: logins: one login recipe per role the plans' [ui] cards name ('as the admin user'): { "role": "admin", "url": "http://localhost:3000/api/login", "userEnv": "ORCH_QA_ADMIN_USER", "passEnv": "ORCH_QA_ADMIN_PASSWORD" }. Names of environment variables only, never their values. The orchestrator's preflight flags a card whose role has no recipe.
